Overall: 7.5/10.

Story & Plot

A cybersecurity expert becomes a whistleblower after uncovering secrets about aliens, putting him on the run from a corporation and a shadowy government agency. Meanwhile, a meteorologist experiencing strange phenomena joins forces with him to prove there is life beyond our understanding. Together, they attempt to expose these cosmic secrets while para-government agents try to stop them by any means necessary.

Comedy & Entertainment

While not primarily a comedy, the film relies on the entertainment value of a fast-paced science-fiction adventure and pop-corn spectacle. It offers an engaging ride rather than a joke-driven script, sweeping viewers up into its high-stakes premise. The narrative focuses squarely on the thrilling journey of its central characters rather than traditional comedic relief.

Performances & Direction

The cast features strong performances anchored by Emily Blunt and Josh O'Connor as they cross paths to reveal extraterrestrial life. Colin Firth takes on the role of a slimy organization head, supported by Eve Hewson and Colman Domingo. Reviewers highlight the strong acting presence across the ensemble as they navigate the fast-paced narrative.

Strengths

  • Expert direction by Steven Spielberg
  • Engaging and fast-paced sci-fi spectacle
  • Strong lead performances from Emily Blunt and Josh O'Connor
  • Entertaining popcorn-movie ride

Weaknesses

Some reviewers note that the film falls short of the big ideas found in earlier alien classics and unfocused rumination can undermine its own intrigue. The narrative runs into structural issues, with a familiar setup and second half that struggle to maintain the tight momentum of the opening acts.

Final verdict

Disclosure Day offers an entertaining and visually sweeping science-fiction ride that brings director Steven Spielberg back to familiar cosmic territory. Though it occasionally stumbles in its broader narrative ambitions and focus, it remains a worthwhile spectacle for fans of alien thrillers. Recommended for viewers looking for an enjoyable, high-stakes cinematic adventure.

Story & Plot

Set in 19th-century British India against the backdrop of the Great Madras Famine of 1876-78, Ranabaali tells the tale of a fierce leader who rises from a drought-stricken land. The period action drama blends faction film genre tropes with colonial trauma to show the extent of British oppression. Director Rahul Sankrityan intersperses his shot scenes with historical images from the 1800s to make his point.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a heavy historical drama centered around famine, colonial trauma, and a grim fight against oppression, the film does not focus on traditional humor. Its entertainment value relies instead on the dramatic scale of its period setting and the confrontation between the characters and colonial rule. Viewers looking for lighthearted moments will find very little levity in this grim historical narrative.

Performances & Direction

Vijay Deverakonda is totally committed to his role as the fierce leader, bringing intense focus and energy to the screen. Rashmika Mandanna also stars in the period drama alongside Arnold Vosloo, who plays Hector. While the lead actor gives his all, some reviews note that the film ultimately becomes all about heroism, missing an opportunity for deeper character exploration.

Strengths

  • Commitment of lead actor Vijay Deverakonda
  • Ambitious period action drama premise
  • Incorporation of historical Great Famine context

Weaknesses

The 2-hour-58-minute runtime puts characters and viewers through a grueling experience that can feel exhausting and unnecessarily violent. Reviewers noted that the pace feels very slow, the second half could have been stronger, and the constant heavy imagery occasionally borders on torture porn.

Final verdict

Ranabaali is a well-intentioned historical period drama that suffers from an overly long runtime, pacing issues, and an exhausting reliance on brutal imagery. While Vijay Deverakonda delivers a dedicated performance, the film ends up being a missed opportunity that might test the patience of mainstream viewers. It comes recommended only for dedicated fans of the lead cast or heavy historical dramas.
